S No  Registrar's order with  Signatures  C482 No. 520 of 2021  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. B.S. Bhandari, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, learned A.G.A. with Mr. Akshay Latwal, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Mr. T.A. Khan, learned senior counsel assisted by Mr. Mohd. Hasnain, learned counsel for the respondent.

4. By the instant C482 application the present applicant is challenging the order dated passed by Civil Judge (J.D.)/ Judicial Magistrate, Haldwani District Nainital in Criminal Complaint Case No.
2535 of 2018, wherein, the present applicant has been summoned for the offences punishable under Sections 504 and 506 of IPC.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
In addition to this, the present applicant is also challenging the order dated 09.03.2021 passed by Second Additional Session Judge Haldwani District Nainital in Criminal Revision No. 22 of 2020.
5.

entities.text: Second Additional Session Judge Haldwani District Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that with the same set of allegations earlier the respondent/complainant moved an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., in which the order was passed for registration of the FIR and thereafter the FIR was registered for the offence punishable under Section 392 of IPC in which after investigation the final report was submitted against which a protest petition was filed and on the protest petition the final report was rejected and the application moved under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. was treated as a complaint as a Complaint Case No. 2535 of 2018 in which applicant was summoned for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 504 and 506 of IPC by an order dated 07.06.2018 against which a revision was allowed and the revisional court observed in the order that the offences punishable under Section C482/520/2021 on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56640106/
1 420, 504 and 506 of IPC are not made out and the matter was remanded back to the Trial Court.

After remand the Trial Court passed a fresh order and summoned the applicant for the offence punishable under Section 504 and 506 IPC against which a revision was filed and the revision was also rejected by the order dated 09.03.2021.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that proceedings as initiated is appears to be a glaring example of abuse of process of law, which is evident from the fact that earlier on the FIR lodged by the respondent/complainant with same set of allegations the final report was filed and not only this at the time when the revisional court remanded the matter the revisional court clearly observed in the order that offences punishable under Section 420, 504 and 506 are not made out.
7. All these aspect required to be considered after inviting counter affidavit.
8. Mr. T.A. Khan, put his appearance on behalf of the respondent and prays for and is granted four weeks' time to file counter affidavit.
9. Two weeks' time is granted to the applicant to file rejoinder affidavit.

For an interim measure, until further order of this court the order dated 09.03.2021 passed in Criminal Revision No. 22 of 2020 by the Additional Session Judge, Haldwani, District Nainital as well as proceeding of Complaint Case No. 2535 of 2018 pending in the court of Civil Judge (J.D.)/Judicial Magistrate, Haldwani, District Nainital, shall remain stayed (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
